title: Multi-Rail Robot Power — Linear (LDO) vs. Switching (Buck) Regulators and Power Budgets

blocks.x: Idea 1: Linear (LDO) regulator heat loss vs. switching (Buck) converter power conservation

items.x: **Primary resource:** [Wikipedia — Buck converter ("Theory" & "Concept")](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buck_converter) `[HTTP 200 — Verified by scripts/check_links.py]`
**What to read:** Read exact headings **`Buck converter`**, **`Theory`**, and **`Idealised case`**.
**What to skip:** Skip discontinuous-mode inductor ripple integrals.
**Key takeaway:** Robots typically carry a $12.0\text{ V}$ battery for motors, but the Arduino Uno and sensors need $5.0\text{ V}$. There are two ways to step $12.0\text{ V}$ down to $5.0\text{ V}$:

**Linear Regulator (`LDO`, like `7805` or `AMS1117`):** Acts like an automatic variable series resistor that drops the extra $12.0 - 5.0 = 7.0\text{ V}$. Input current equals output current ($I_{\text{in}} = I_{\text{load}}$), and all the dropped voltage turns straight into heat: $P_{\text{heat}} = (V_{\text{in}} - V_{\text{out}}) \cdot I_{\text{load}}$. Great for tiny currents ($\le 50\text{ mA}$), but at $0.50\text{ A}$ it burns $7.0 \times 0.50 = 3.50\text{ W}$ and cooks itself!

**Switching Step-Down (`Buck`) Converter:** Uses a fast PWM switch, an inductor, and a capacitor to convert high voltage at low current into low voltage at higher current with efficiency $\eta \approx 0.90$ ($90\%$): $P_{\text{in}} = \frac{P_{\text{out}}}{\eta} \implies I_{\text{in}} = \frac{V_{\text{out}} \cdot I_{\text{load}}}{\eta \cdot V_{\text{in}}}$.

**Alternative resource:** [Falstad Circuit Simulator — Buck Converter](https://www.falstad.com/circuit/circuitjs.html) `[verify in-app]` — Open `Circuits` $\rightarrow$ `Power Converters` $\rightarrow$ `Buck Converter` `[verify in-app]`.

blocks.x: Idea 2: System worst-case power budgeting and separate motor vs. logic voltage rails

items.x: **Primary resource:** [SparkFun — How to Power a Project](https://learn.sparkfun.com/tutorials/how-to-power-a-project) `[HTTP 200 — Verified by scripts/check_links.py]`
**What to read:** Review how portable projects budget battery voltage and current capacity across high-draw actuators and logic electronics.
**What to skip:** Skip solar panel charging circuits.
**Key takeaway:** Never power a motor from the Arduino Uno's onboard `5V` pin! Instead, split your robot into two power rails fed from the main $12.0\text{ V}$ battery:
**Raw $12.0\text{ V}$ Motor Rail (`VMOT`):** Feeds the H-bridge motor drivers directly.

**Regulated $5.0\text{ V}$ Logic Rail (`VCC`):** Stepped down from $12.0\text{ V}$ via a **Buck converter** to feed the Arduino and sensors cleanly. A **power budget** sums the worst-case (stall) currents on every rail so you can size your regulator and main battery fuse with a safe margin.

**Alternative resource:** [SparkFun — Electric Power](https://learn.sparkfun.com/tutorials/electric-power) `[HTTP 200 — Verified by scripts/check_links.py]` — Review exact headings **`What is Electric Power?`** and **`Calculating Power`**.

blocks.x: Compare stepping $V_{\text{in}} = 12.0\text{ V}$ down to $V_{\text{out}} = 5.0\text{ V}$ for a $5.0\text{ V}$ logic and sensor rail drawing $I_{\text{load}} = 0.50\text{ A}$ ($P_{\text{out}} = 5.0 \times 0.50 = 2.50\text{ W}$). A **Linear Regulator (`LDO`)** passes the full load current straight from the $12.0\text{ V}$ battery ($I_{\text{in}} = I_{\text{load}} = 0.50\text{ A}$) and burns the entire $7.0\text{ V}$ voltage drop as heat ($3.50\text{ W}$). By contrast, a switching **Buck Converter** ($\eta = 90\%$) conserves power across its inductor-capacitor stage, drawing only $I_{\text{buck,in}} = 0.231\text{ A}$ from the $12.0\text{ V}$ battery and wasting just $0.28\text{ W}$:

blocks.tex: P_{\text{LDO,heat}} = (V_{\text{in}} - V_{\text{out}}) \cdot I_{\text{load}}, \qquad I_{\text{buck,in}} = \frac{V_{\text{out}} \cdot I_{\text{load}}}{\eta \cdot V_{\text{in}}}, \qquad P_{\text{buck,heat}} = V_{\text{in}} \cdot I_{\text{buck,in}} - V_{\text{out}} \cdot I_{\text{load}}

blocks.x: In `TODO 1`, the LDO drops `v_in - v_out = 7.0 V` at `i_load = 0.50 A`, wasting `7.0 * 0.50 = 3.50 W`. The buck converter delivers `p_out = v_out * i_load = 2.50 W` at `90%` efficiency, so `p_in = (v_out * i_load) / buck_eff` and `i_buck_in = p_in / v_in`.

def compare_ldo_vs_buck(v_in, v_out, i_load, buck_eff=0.90):
    p_ldo_heat = (v_in - v_out) * i_load
    i_buck_in = (v_out * i_load) / (buck_eff * v_in)
    p_buck_heat = (v_in * i_buck_in) - (v_out * i_load)
    return p_ldo_heat, i_buck_in, p_buck_heat

def compare_ldo_vs_buck(v_in, v_out, i_load, buck_eff=0.90):
    p_ldo_heat = (v_in - v_out) * i_load
    i_buck_in = (v_out * i_load) / (buck_eff * v_in)
    p_buck_heat = (v_in * i_buck_in) - (v_out * i_load)
    return p_ldo_heat, i_buck_in, p_buck_heat


def worst_case_battery_budget(i_motor_stall, i_buck_in, safety_factor=1.25):
    i_total_peak = i_motor_stall + i_buck_in
    fuse_rating_a = i_total_peak * safety_factor
    return i_total_peak, fuse_rating_a


p_ldo, i_buck, p_buck = compare_ldo_vs_buck(12.0, 5.0, 0.50, buck_eff=0.90)
i_peak, fuse_a = worst_case_battery_budget(i_motor_stall=3.00, i_buck_in=i_buck)

print(f"LDO heat loss : {p_ldo:.2f} W (at 12V -> 5V, 0.50 A)")
print(f"Buck input    : {i_buck:.3f} A | Buck heat loss: {p_buck:.2f} W")
print(f"Battery peak  : {i_peak:.3f} A | Recommended fuse (1.25x): {fuse_a:.2f} A")

items.x: **Powering a hobby servo or DC motor from the Arduino Uno's onboard $5\text{ V}$ linear regulator (`VIN` fed by $12\text{ V}$):** When the servo stalls at $1.0\text{ A}$, the tiny onboard LDO has to dissipate $(12 - 5) \times 1.0 = 7.0\text{ W}$, causing immediate thermal shutdown and rebooting the Arduino! Always use an external Buck converter for $5\text{ V}$ servos and logic.

**Assuming Buck converter input current equals output current:** Because a Buck converter conserves power ($V_{\text{in}} I_{\text{in}} \approx V_{\text{out}} I_{\text{out}} / \eta$), stepping $12\text{ V}$ down to $5\text{ V}$ draws **less** current from the $12\text{ V}$ battery than the $5\text{ V}$ load consumes!

**LDO heat calculation:** You power an Arduino Uno + sensors drawing $200\text{ mA}$ ($0.20\text{ A}$) at $5.0\text{ V}$ from a $9.0\text{ V}$ battery through a linear regulator (`LDO`). How many Watts of heat does the LDO dissipate? Answer

**Why separate `VMOT` and `VCC` rails?** Why do we connect the H-bridge motor supply (`VMOT`) directly to the $12\text{ V}$ battery while feeding the Arduino `5V` rail through a separate Buck regulator? Answer

blocks.x: Separating the rails keeps multi-amp motor stall surges off the $5.0\text{ V}$ regulator so the microcontroller's logic voltage stays steady at $5.0\text{ V}$ even when the motor stalls.

items.x: A **Linear Regulator (`LDO`)** wastes $P_{\text{heat}} = (V_{\text{in}} - V_{\text{out}}) \cdot I_{\text{load}}$ as heat, whereas a **Switching (`Buck`) Converter** steps voltage down at $\sim 90\%$ efficiency ($I_{\text{in}} = \frac{V_{\text{out}} I_{\text{load}}}{\eta V_{\text{in}}}$).
A **system power budget** separates high-current motor power (`VMOT`) from regulated logic power (`VCC`) and sums worst-case stall currents to size fuses and supplies safely.
